text: The first test iron ingot hissed white vapor in cold water. Ore ratios, coal expenditure, and the cost of smoke exhaust were all entered in the process manual.
Gears and bearings meshed with perfect precision. The community can finally machine its own mechanical parts.
The filament in the glass bulb lit up. Power must still be produced continuously, and machines must be wired according to their load.

The exposed walls of the old quarry reveal red-brown layers of iron ore. In another ravine beyond the ridge, an exposed coal seam has not yet been soaked through by groundwater.

Hydro, wind, and biomass can all power small generators. Choose the local grid route without mining or burning coal for power.
Grounding, circuit breakers, and regular inspections make power a reliable public service; once complete, you can establish an electricity and communications office.
Permanent radio stations have taken over the messengers' legwork. Intercity departures require an on-duty dispatcher and a reliable power supply, rather than repeated manual requests.
Medical staff use medicine and power to vaccinate residents while on duty; public health begins to shift from treating illness to preventing it.
Recycled scrap iron is machined into standard mechanical parts; the public route can also produce parts locally without forcing mining.

An electrified freight network and dispatch center now link the old stations; one-way trips for new freight orders along the lakeshores between the two cities have fallen from 180 seconds to 45 seconds. Freight, travel rations, return trips, and onboard drivers are still allocated by the rules.
Allocate power based on stock levels and minimum public needs; workshops switch to automated batching, and the administration can manage Old Town's daily schedules.
The experimental cohort expends teaching aids and electricity to compile knowledge that can withstand review, paving the way for an advanced experimental community in the future.
Vaccination, medical care, and schools now have continuously archived registers. The handover of cross-city public services no longer hangs on the lifespan of the older generation of founders.
A small controller production line turns components and knowledge into stocked goods, drawing a safe boundary for the future introduction of audited autonomous machines.
Electric furnaces smelt recovered iron for trial production of specialty alloys. Blueprints are only blueprints; the metal still has to be smelted furnace by furnace in the workshops.
Battery banks can withstand brief power fluctuations, but the system will still shut down once they are depleted; Old Town's generators can be set to prioritize essential services or manufacturing.

Power for advanced facilities, clinical care, accountability, and replacement staffing are integrated; while opening a new form of communal life, everyone retains the right to refuse bodily modification.
